As rain lashed the Pir Panjal mountains before dawn on 19 July, Haji Mohammad Latief stepped outside his home in Murrah, a remote mountain village in Indian-administered Kashmir. His daughter had asked him to move the family’s car to a safer place as the rain got heavier.
“I had only just parked it,” Latief recalled. “When I turned around, I saw the water coming.” Minutes later, a cloudburst sent mud, boulders and water crashing down the hillside.
Latief, 48, had spent years building the house, where five generations of his Gujjar family lived together. Within minutes, the torrent swallowed it, trapping eight family members inside. He survived only because he had stepped outside. By dawn, everything he had built lay in rubble.
When the Guardian reached Murrah four days later, electricity, roads and mobile networks were cut off. Floodwaters had washed away roads and footbridges, leaving the only way into the village a 90-minute walk through rain and landslide debris. Residents carried sacks of flour, cooking gas cylinders and medicines across the broken crossing.
Murrah is perched high in the Pir Panjal range above the town of Bafliaz, in Poonch district, about 125 miles (200km) south-west of Srinagar, Kashmir’s main city. The village is home to mostly Gujjars, one of the largest pastoralist communities in the Himalayas, whose livelihoods have long depended on livestock, farming and seasonal migration through the mountains.
The hillside remained too unstable for excavators to reach. Soldiers, disaster response teams and local volunteers searched the debris by hand while others combed the swollen Suran River for the missing.
Latief now lives in the house of his brother, Mohd Bashir, just above the landslide. Inside, women gathered to mourn while men quietly received visitors offering condolences. Verses from the Qur’an echoed through the house.
“I built that house for my family,” Latief said, holding up pictures of his 16-year-old son Sajjad Ahmed, an aspiring cricketer, whose body was still missing. Days before the disaster, the family recorded videos together.
As mourners gathered, news spread that another body had been found several miles down the river; the room fell silent as another funeral procession passed through the village.
Among those searching was Mohammad Razak, 45, who had spent four days combing the river with a team of volunteers. “We’ve been searching every bend of the river,” he said. “We’re still hoping we’ll find them.”
Murrah was among the worst-hit places after a series of cloudbursts, flash floods and landslides swept Jammu and Kashmir this month, killing at least 28 people. Scientists say rising temperatures are increasing the likelihood of short, intense rainfall events across the western Himalayas. In steep mountainous terrain, these rains can trigger rapid flooding and landslides, putting remote communities at increased risk. For mountain communities, the climate crisis is also exacerbating longstanding geographical and social vulnerabilities.
The destruction stretched far beyond Murrah. About 30 miles away in Rajouri, the Manawar Tawi River burst its banks, washing away roads, dozens of vehicles and the town’s main Bela bus station.
Low-lying settlements along the riverbank were submerged in mud and debris. Several houses collapsed across the Pir Panjal mountains, livestock were swept away and hundreds of families were displaced.
About 180 miles north, in Gurez Valley near the line of control with Pakistan-administered Kashmir, residents say they are seeing the same pattern. A cloudburst in Achoora village on 20 July damaged the crops of 11 families and blocked the valley’s only road.
Residents say increasingly erratic rainfall is disrupting farming and making traditional livelihoods more precarious. It followed a series of cloudbursts that hit Gurez and neighbouring Tulail over the past month, damaging homes, farmland, bridges, and roads.
“People knew when the snow would come and when to plant crops,” said Aamir Asghar Khan, 26, a resident of Achoora. “Nothing seems predictable any more. The rain is getting more intense every year, and the frequent cloudbursts are threatening our livelihoods.”
Heavy rainfall also triggered devastating floods and landslides in Ladakh and across the border in Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan, reinforcing concerns that increasingly erratic weather is affecting communities across the western Himalayas.
The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (Icimod) said the western Himalayas were experiencing frequent bursts of intense rainfall capable of triggering floods, landslides and cloudbursts. Accelerating glacier melt is likely to increase flood risks in the short term before reducing water availability in coming decades.
“The challenge our mountain communities face is twofold – too much water at times and too little at others,” an expert from Icimod said. “Adaptation requires work on both fronts, managing flood risk and water scarcity together.”
ICIMOD said priorities included expanding community-based early warning systems, installing more weather stations in high-altitude areas, restoring damaged watersheds and designing roads and other infrastructure for future weather conditions rather than historical weather patterns.
Dr Suheel Rasool Mir, a Kashmir-based sociologist who studies Indigenous communities in Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh, said pastoral communities were among the first to bear the consequences of erratic weather as their livelihoods relied directly on forests, rivers, grazing lands and seasonal migration.
“For Gujjar, Bakarwal and Dard-Shin communities, these disasters are not simply natural hazards,” he said. “As climate extremes become more frequent, they lose not only homes and livestock but also the ecological knowledge and ancestral livelihoods that have sustained them for generations.”
For Latief back in Murrah, only one hope remained. “I just want to find them,” he said. “Then we can bury our family together.”

Banihal, Aug 19: Deputy Commissioners of Ramban and Udhampur, along with senior district officials, on Wednesday visited the headquarters of the Sawalkote Hydroelectric Project at Tanger in Ramban to review the progress and current status of the ambitious 1,800 MW project.
The Sawalkote Hydroelectric Project, being developed by NHPC Limited, is set to become one of the biggest hydropower projects in Jammu and Kashmir. The delegation was led by Ramban Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Alyas Khan and Udhampur Deputy Commissioner Minga Sherpa.
Head of the Sawalkote Hydroelectric Project, Satnam Singh, briefed the visiting officials about the overall development of the project, including key infrastructure components, dam works, access tunnels and roads. He also outlined the project's forward roadmap and the regulatory milestones required before the commencement of major construction activities.
According to NHPC, the project is expected to move forward after approval from the Public Investment Board (PIB), followed by clearance from the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), after which tenders for the project are scheduled to be opened.
During the visit, the officials were given a video tour of the project site and a detailed presentation covering its power generation capacity, tunnel works, proposed submergence area, ongoing construction-related activities, future development plans and the Social Impact Assessment (SIA).
The district administration officials appreciated the progress and efforts being made to formally kick-start construction of the project and assured NHPC of full support and cooperation for its timely execution.
The delegation included District Forest Officer Udhampur Sandeep Divyajyoti Behera, District Mining Officer Udhampur Sunil Sharma, Additional Deputy Commissioner and Collector Sawalkote Project Shokat Hayat Mattoo, besides other revenue and police officials.
As part of the visit, the officials also participated in a symbolic tree plantation activity, which NHPC said reflected its commitment towards environmental protection, biodiversity conservation and sustainable development.

Man City in advanced talks for £85m Bouaddi, 18
- Published
Manchester City are in advanced talks with Lille over a move for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.
The Premier League side want to conclude the transfer this week after agreeing to sell Rodri to Barcelona.
It is understood Lille value the 18-year-old at 100 million euros (£85.6m).
Bouaddi impressed at this summer's World Cup - starting five of Morocco's six matches in their run to the quarter-finals - after a starring role in Lille's Champions League victory over Real Madrid in 2024 announced him on the big stage.
He functions as a deep-lying conductor and would complement summer signing Elliot Anderson, who is comfortable as a box-to-box midfielder as well as the number six role he plays for England.
Bouaddi has played 88 times for Lille since making his debut in October 2023, three days after his 16th birthday, and helped them finish third in Ligue 1 last season.
Spain captain Rodri is set to complete a £65m move to Barcelona in the coming days on a four-year contract.
The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner has made 298 appearances across seven trophy-laden seasons at City after joining from Atletico Madrid in 2019 for a then club record £62.8m.
The 30-year-old missed much of the 2024-25 campaign with a serious knee injury, and parts of last season were disrupted by a hamstring issue.
However, he was back to his best at the World Cup in the summer, leading Spain to their second global title and being named player of the tournament.

Valve Steam Frame videos show how to wear the headset, perfect the fit and sign in
Eight leaked Steam Frame videos are informative and kinda silly.
Usually we hate it when a Valve starts leaking, but right now, we're pretty OK with it. Valve accidentally published eight videos about the Steam Frame VR headset in an ARM Steam Client update today, and before the how-tos could be removed, they were spotted, saved and shared by users. So, Valve published some and is letting the rest run wild online.
There's no shocking new information in the videos, but they do offer an in-depth look at the Steam Frame sign-in process, how to wear the headset and what accessories come with it. The videos are all clean, friendly and slightly silly, as if directed by a pre-homicidal GLaDOS. The sign-in video is particularly tongue-in-cheek, showing an optional, lowkey ridiculous process that allows you to scan a QR login code by focusing your phone camera on one lens of the headset. The basic fit video also shows people wearing the Steam Frame over their mouths or as a purse. It's so crazzzzzzzy.
The most interesting videos show the interpupillary distance wheel, which features a sliding lock, and the ergonomic accessories. These include hand straps for the controllers, an additional support strap that runs across the crown of the head, and an extended light blocker for players with small noses. The Steam Frame's squishy face gasket and optional eye spacer attach to the headset with magnets for easy modularity, and the charging port lives in a battery pack on the backside of the main head strap.

One thing that wasn't included in today's video dump was the headset's price, which is poised to be quite high, considering the ongoing RAM shortage that's driving up costs across the computer hardware space. The Spanish government has U-turned and said it will allow 500 migrant children in Ceuta to relocate to the mainland.
The majority of the estimated 70,000 people who crossed into Ceuta – a Spanish territory on the coast of north Africa – on 30 July have returned to Morocco. However, under Spanish law, the state has a duty of care to young, unaccompanied migrants until they reach the age of 18.
On 13 August, the interior minister, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, had said: “Anyone who illegally enters Ceuta or Melilla [another Spanish enclave in north Africa] knows they will be sent back because Spain and Morocco work together to this end. They will not reach the peninsula, nor the European continent and nor will they remain indefinitely in Ceuta or Melilla.”
The transfer of the children to the Spanish mainland is a sensitive political topic as several regions governed jointly by the conservative People’s party and the far-right Vox are reluctant or opposed to receiving their quota.
To minimise conflict, the youth ministry, in coordination with the Ceuta government, is devising an urgent plan under which NGOs and child protection agencies take charge of the most vulnerable children, girls in particular, without transferring their guardianship to Spain’s regional governments.
Rubén Pérez Correa, the secretary of state for children, has been in Ceuta since Sunday in an effort to resolve a situation in which hundreds of children are living on the street and existing on handouts from Ceuta residents.
News of the government’s plan came only hours after the European Commission said that under EU law all of the migrants should be returned to Morocco. Asked to clarify, the commission’s spokesperson on internal affairs, Markus Lammert, said that by law all irregular migrants remaining in Ceuta should be sent back, “including unaccompanied minors”.
The People’s party has rejected the government plan, saying the best place for the children is with their families. “If Morocco has asked for the children to be returned and if Europe says the illegal immigrants should all be returned, whether children or not, what more does the government need?” the People’s party deputy finance spokesperson, Juan Bravo, said in a television interview.
The mixed messages partly derive from the fact the latest European pact on immigration has not yet been incorporated into Spanish law and therefore Spain’s own legislation on the treatment of unaccompanied minors remains in force.
According to Spain’s ministry of inclusion and migration, as of last March 21,104 people aged 16-23 were guardians of the state, of whom about 3,500 were under 17. Approximately 50% were from Morocco. Girls made up about 8% of the total.

Ever since the MacBook Neo was announced this spring, I've been looking for a serious alternative. Not a cheap knockoff that sacrifices quality for price. No, no. I was hunting for a Windows laptop with the same goal as the MacBook Neo—hiding its compromises and delivering an otherwise premium laptop at a lower cost. For months, it was crickets.
Then, the Dell XPS 13 showed up on my doorstep, and it understood the assignment. For many reasons, this was the one I'd been waiting for. But the question remains: Is it actually the better budget laptop? The answer surprised me when I dug into the testing.
Hidden Compromises
When the MacBook Neo was originally announced, it was a shocker. Apple coming in at the $599 price point for the base configuration felt unreal. Apple had never in its history brought the MacBook to such a low price. Even at its new $699 starting price, it's in unprecedented territory. Importantly, this encroached on the territory of Windows laptops, where it has traditionally had a monopoly.
And while many Windows laptops are available at this price, they suffer from many of the same problems, such as cheap materials or corners cut with low-quality displays and touchpads. Even a cheap laptop I like quite a bit, like the HP OmniBook 5 (with the Snapdragon X Plus), has a weak point in its touchpad.
But the Dell XPS 13 sought to match the MacBook Neo's premium quality in nearly every aspect. It has the same starting price of $699 (or $599 for students). It's exactly the same size at just a half-inch thick, so when the lid is closed and you're holding it, it feels just as portable. The XPS 13 weighs 2.2 pounds, half a pound lighter than the MacBook Neo. The Neo isn't heavy, but holding both in your hands, the difference is noticeable. That's the first point in favor of the XPS 13.
Despite a slightly smaller screen (13 inches, measured diagonally), the MacBook Neo sits taller than the XPS 13 when the lid is open. That's because the XPS 13's 13.4-inch display is surrounded by much smaller bezels—particularly the bottom, which gives the XPS 13 a more modern look. The white keyboard and flashier color options of the MacBook Neo certainly have their appeal, especially since the XPS 13 comes in only two shades of silver. But in general, more screen real estate and smaller dimensions are preferable, especially if you want to travel on an airplane with your laptop.
And then there's the screen itself. Most $700 laptops have mediocre screens that aren't bright enough and have poor colors. I never expected Apple to skimp on the display, of course, and it didn't. It goes up to 509 nits (as tested) and has decent color reproduction. But the XPS 13 is better in three ways. First, it has a touchscreen, which MacBooks don't (yet) have. That's a nice addition for an entry-level model. It also has a 120-Hz refresh rate, which gives the screen fast, fluid responsiveness that not even the MacBook Air has. Again, that's a feature that's exceedingly rare to find on a budget-level laptop. Lastly, the XPS 13 has better color saturation, specifically on the Adobe RGB and P3 color scales. It's actually one of the better IPS screens I've tested on a laptop, and it's as sharp as the MacBook Neo.
None of these are weak points of the MacBook Neo, but it's worth noting that the XPS 13 has it beat in a number of these areas. That's also true of the keyboard and trackpad. Both are excellent on these laptops, and I found myself comfortable using them right off the bat. Again, trackpads in particular can be a sore spot for budget Windows laptops, but Dell smartly didn't skimp on it. Apple's the one that compromised on the keyboard, both by not including Touch ID in the base model and by removing backlighting (which the XPS 13 includes).
Ports, Storage, and Videoconferencing
I already mentioned the display and the portability, but there are a few other places where the XPS 13 is the clear winner. The first is the USB-C ports. Both devices have two, but the XPS 13 splits them, so one is on the left side, and one is on the right side. I really like this decision, as it allows you to charge the device from either side. Then, there's the speed of these USB-C ports. One of the USB-C ports on the MacBook Neo is an outdated USB 2 port. Not only is it slow for file transfers, but it also can't natively output to an external display. Both USB-C ports on the XPS 13 are USB 3.2 Gen 2, which can each support a 4K display and transfer data at up to 10 Gbps.
The Neo does have an advantage when it comes to ports, though. It has a headphone jack, whereas the XPS 13 doesn't. This might be less of a big deal today than it was in the past, but I prefer laptops to keep them.
The XPS 13 comes with 512 GB of storage in both the base and upgraded models. The MacBook Neo base model comes only with 256 GB, and you'll need to upgrade to the Touch ID model for 521 GB. On top of that, Dell's laptop uses faster storage. That's a winning combination.
The videoconferencing setup is similarly good. Both webcams are 1080p. Though the image processing is a bit better on the MacBook Neo, the XPS 13 includes an IR camera for logging in without a password. The base configuration of the Neo doesn't have Touch ID, so you have to type a password to log in, change settings, and pay online.
The RAM Problem
Apple never claimed the MacBook Neo was a powerhouse. Built on an iPhone chip (the A18 Pro) and limited to 8 GB of RAM, it is clearly designed for college students and anyone with lower-level computing needs. When I tested it initially, I found that if I wasn't paying attention, it was easy to let open applications, tons of browser tabs, and background tasks slow the computer down, with the main bottleneck being the 8 GB of RAM. Apple hasn't sold a MacBook with 8 GB of RAM since 2024, but the company has always insisted that its unified memory system means it doesn't need as much capacity as a Windows PC. But is that really true? Now that we have a very comparable Windows system with 8 GB of RAM as well, it'll be easy to test just how true Apple's claims are.
The bad news is that both devices took very little effort to use up the available memory. Playing a YouTube video with various news sites open in six Google Chrome tabs was enough to use over 90 percent of the 8 GB. Neither Windows nor macOS feels optimized for a computer with just 8 GB of RAM these days, no doubt from all the AI-infused tasks running in the background. Now, just because you're getting dangerously close to reaching 100 percent of the memory utilization, that doesn't mean your computer instantly freezes up. It takes a lot to get these systems to grind to a halt, but with a 16-GB laptop, you'll spend much less time managing what tabs and applications you have open. On the other hand, if you're a student coming from a cheap Chromebook or hand-me-down computer, these laptops will feel like a nice upgrade.
The XPS 13 has a fan inside, while the MacBook Neo is passively cooled. Under a heavy load you can hear that fan spin up in the XPS 13, whereas the Neo is completely silent. Both laptops get excellent battery life—enough to get through a full day of class or work. That's another area where laptops at this price tended to suffer in the past.
But the big difference between these two laptops is how you can configure them. Both start at $700 ($699 for the Neo, to be exact), and you get one upgrade option. For an extra $100, you can move up to the MacBook Neo with 512 GB of storage and Touch ID built in. On the other hand, the Dell XPS 13 has a $900 model that's identical to the base model, except it has 16 GB of RAM. So yes, the 16-GB version of the XPS 13 is $100 more expensive. But it's better in nearly every way, and it's likely the best laptop you can buy for less than $1,000.
And even when comparing the 8-GB model, the XPS 13 handily beats the MacBook Neo in tons of small ways. It has a better display, a backlit keyboard, two USB ports—one on each side—that support charging and 4K monitors, and it's more portable. It does all that while looking super sharp and feeling just as premium as the Neo. While I think everyone should buy a 16-GB laptop, at the 8-GB level, the Dell XPS 13 is the better laptop no matter how you slice it.

Thai teen found in suitcase died from suffocation, police reveal
- Published
A 17-year-old girl whose body was found in a suitcase in Thailand died from suffocation, according to authorities.
Police in the coastal city of Pattaya previously said they had found Tunchanok Donhomla's naked body in a bag near a railway track in the early hours of 27 June.
This was just 15 minutes after they had arrested 45-year-old Australian man Simon Peter Carman, who was allegedly "preparing to flee the country", they said.
On Wednesday, Pattaya City police chief Anek Srathongyoo told the BBC that Tunchanok's autopsy results "showed she died from suffocation".
"She also suffered some brain injury but that was not the cause of death," he added. "It could have happened after she died as the accused moved her body in a suitcase before dumping it."
Anek further revealed that the DNA found on Tunchanok's body matched Carman's, and suggested that it "likely came from when he put her body in the suitcase".
Police are pressing four charges against Carman: murder; concealing or moving the body; kidnapping a child over 15 but under 18; and taking away a child over 15 but under 18 for an indecent act.
"[Carman] did not completely deny all the charges initially," Anek said. "He admitted to taking her out. That said, even if he pleads not guilty in court later, I believe we have collected all the evidence thoroughly and closed every loophole in the case in order to prove it to the court that he has committed those crimes."
Police will be ready to submit the case to prosecutors by Friday, according to Anek, who noted that the deadline for them to indict Carman was 18 September.
Previously released CCTV footage allegedly showed Carman entering a condominium with Tunchanok at 03:34 local time on 25 June. Later that evening, he emerged alone "carrying a large suitcase", according to a police statement.
The statement said Carman loaded the bag onto a motorbike before driving towards a railway line.
Following his arrest, Carman denied the charges against him and claimed he had acted in self defence.
He reportedly told police he had agreed to pay Tunchanok 1,000 baht ($30; £23) for sexual services, but they had had an argument when they returned to his apartment and he had offered only 500 baht.
In a video recorded while he was in custody, the suspect issued a message to Tunchanok's family, saying: "I feel bad for what happened to your daughter. It was out of my control."
"I know you'll be very sad, upset… same [as] me," he added. "Please tell other girls… just to be careful."
Tunchanok's family previously told the ABC she was an only child who lived with her father and step-mother in the province of Kalasin, about 480km (298 miles) north-east of Pattaya.
The teen, whose nickname was Cake, had told her parents she wanted to go on holiday with a friend, and had travelled to Pattaya on 16 June.
Her father, Thongchai Donhomla, said he was "deeply saddened" by his daughter's death.
"My daughter had no mother, so whenever she wanted anything, she would find a way herself, and she always helped me too," he told a local reporter.
Her stepmother, Oradee Bussarakum, said that the news of Tunchanok's death had confirmed their fears.
"We were scared. We just hoped it wouldn't turn out the way we feared," she said. "Now our eyes are swollen from crying."
"I just want [Carman] executed," she added. "I even asked the police if I could hit him, if I could beat him."
If convicted of murder, Carman could face the death penalty.

Politically finished, scared of Congress: Rahul Gandhi targets PM at CWC meeting
At the Congress Working Committee meeting, Rahul Gandhi attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and set out the party's political line. The discussion widened to youth unrest, Ayodhya donation allegations, China concerns and women's reservation.
Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi told the Congress Working Committee (CWC) meeting on Wednesday that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was “politically finished” and had “come to his knees”, according to sources. Gandhi said the government’s “time is over” and urged Congress workers to remain proud of the party’s ideology, claiming that Modi was “only scared of the Congress”.
The remarks came during a four-hour CWC meeting at Indira Bhavan in New Delhi, where the party discussed paper leaks, alleged irregularities in Ram temple donations, China’s alleged incursions in Arunachal Pradesh, E20 fuel and women’s reservation. The Congress also decided to take the paper leak and “chanda chori” issues to the grassroots through nationwide campaigns.
CONGRESS TO TAKE PAPER LEAK ISSUE TO GRASSROOTS
The CWC expressed concern over unemployment and alleged failures in the education and examination system, with party chief Mallikarjun Kharge accusing the Modi government of “destroying” the future of students.
The party said its ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ campaign will now be expanded to nearly 800 cities to raise issues affecting students. Rahul Gandhi will participate in some of these programmes.
The four Congress chief ministers have also been asked to prepare reports on reforms required in their respective education and examination systems and submit them to Kharge within a month.
The CWC alleged that at least 152 paper leak cases have been reported since 2014 and accused the government of using excessive force against student protesters. It also criticised the handling of the NEET controversy and demanded greater accountability in the education system.
RAM TEMPLE DONATION ROW: SC-MONITORED PROBE SOUGHT
The Congress also decided to take its allegations of “chanda chori” linked to donations for the Ram temple in Ayodhya to the village and panchayat level.
The CWC demanded an independent probe into the allegations under the supervision of the Supreme Court, along with a comprehensive audit of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust’s accounts and assets, including cash and valuables.
The party accused the BJP of using the Ram temple issue for political mobilisation and questioned the Centre’s attempt to distance itself from the matter.
CONGRESS TARGETS GOVT OVER CHINA, E20
The CWC accused the government of following a “surrender policy” towards China and raised concerns over alleged Chinese incursions in Arunachal Pradesh.
It claimed that PLA personnel had restricted Indian access to some patrolling points and traditional grazing areas along the Line of Actual Control. The party also criticised the government over what it described as failures in foreign policy.
The Congress reiterated concerns over E20 petrol, including lower mileage, compatibility issues, fuel contamination, loss of consumer choice and the environmental impact of diverting sugarcane and maize towards ethanol production.
WOMEN’S QUOTA, VOTING SEATS AND VANDE MATARAM
The CWC reiterated its demand for immediate implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha based on the existing strength of 543 seats, beginning with the 2029 elections.
It also demanded that the constitutional freeze on the current strength of the Lok Sabha and its allocation among states be extended for another 25 years.
Separately, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said the party had decided that only the first two stanzas of ‘Vande Mataram’ would be sung at all future Congress events, in accordance with a 1937 resolution of the party’s highest decision-making body.
The Congress also termed the recently concluded Monsoon Session of Parliament a “success” for the Opposition, saying it had jointly raised issues that kept the government on the back foot.

Quick Summary
Apple Maps uses simple icons for search, directions, map modes, current location, weather, saved places, offline maps, sharing ETA, reporting incidents, and more. This guide explains every symbol and button across the app’s main screens.
Apple Maps has steadily improved over the years, but it still needs to catch up with Google Maps, especially in places like global coverage, public transport options, offline navigation, real-time traffic data, and much more. But if you are using an iPhone, unless you use Google Maps even on iOS, like me, Apple Maps is the default and the best choice for most people.
Apple Maps is cleaner and more properly integrated with the other Apple ecosystems. If you live in a place where Apple Maps goes one-on-one with Google Maps, then you shouldn’t even look further than Apple Maps for your navigation.
However, if you are a beginner or switching to Apple Maps from Google Maps, some icons and features can be confusing at first. Thanks to Apple, which kept the interface simpler, you don’t need an enormous learning curve to know how to use it. Most of the features are easy, and the icons are easily recognizable, but this guide helps you go even further by guiding you to know what every icon and feature means in Apple Maps.
This is a very comprehensive guide. It includes every Apple Maps screen and the meaning of every icon on each screen. You can also bookmark this page. In the future, if you get stuck on any icon you are wondering about, you can simply open this page and get to know what that icon means.
Table of Contents
What Do All the Icons and Symbols in Apple Maps Mean?
Apple Maps Home Screen Icon Meanings
- Map Options: Using this, you can change the Apple Maps options. Currently, Apple Maps supports Driving, Public Transport, Satellite, Explore, and much more. Also, depending on your selection, the map icon changes.
- Recenter Map: When you are navigating, you can recenter your position.
- Profile Menu: Tapping on your profile picture reveals the places you saved, reports, offline maps, your preferences, and much more.
- Voice Search: You can use the voice mode to search for places. This is just a voice mode and not a voice assistant.
- Search Maps: This is the main search bar for the maps where you can search for places, destinations, and much more.
- Compass: Apple Maps also comes with a native compass option that lets you easily find which direction you are pointing to. It only appears when you rotate the map and tap on it, pointing to the north direction.
- Weather & Air Quality: It shows the current temperature and local AQI for any location you are pointing to.
- Current Location: This shows your current location, and it blinks slightly, and the shadow cone is the direction you are pointing to.
Apple Maps Profile Screen
- Profile Menu: This is the same profile icon you see before swiping up for more details.
- Saved Places: Here you can view Home, Work, and saved places.
- Your Guides: Similarly, in this section you can see and open favorites and saved guides.
- Share My Location: A quick button lets you perform various tasks; the Share your current location button allows you to instantly share your current location.
- Mark My Location: This button instantly saves your current location.
- Report an Issue: This helps you report a Maps issue; you can report incidents, route issues, street issues, and much more.
Apple Maps Search Screen
- Search Maps: The main search bar allows you to search for different places with suggestions below.
- Voice Search: Use your voice; this is a speech-to-text converter, not a voice assistant.
- Close Search: You can close the search.
- Find Nearby: These are the default recommendations that all Apple Maps users see.
Apple Maps Place Details Screen
- Share Place: If you are looking at any particular location, you can tap on the share to share it with your friends or family.
- Close Details: Close the details card about this place.
- Download Map: You can save the map offline, but use it if you want to use your maps offline, especially when there is no internet in the place you are visiting.
- Directions: You can get directions to this place; it already shows you the current driving mode and the time to get there.
- Place Information: You can use the key details about the place, including its popular name, elevation, area, and much more.
- Add to Library: You can save this place.
- Add to Favorites: You can mark this place as a favorite.
- More Options: Open more place actions.
Related: If you are confused about symbols on Apple Maps, you can check our detailed guide on Apple Map icons
Apple Maps Place Options Menu
- Travel Time: Tapping on the three-dot button also reveals more places along with other information; first, it shows the current driving mode, and also the time to get to that location.
- Add to Places: Next, you can add the place to your favorites. You can simply tap on “Add to Places.”
- Add to Guides: You can also add this place to the guides. For those who are not aware, guides contain multiple places.
- Add a Note: You can add a Note about the place.
- Favorite: You can mark the place as a favorite.
- Pin: You can pin this place.
- Share: You can also share the place by tapping on the three-dot menu and tapping on the share option.
- Report an Issue: Report a problem here, such as the name is wrong, the address or location map is wrong, the hours are wrong, the closed category is wrong, and much more.
Apple Maps Directions Screen
- Driving: This is a part of Apple Maps direction options. Driving includes mostly the car option.
- Walking: Get directions if you want to go on foot.
- Public Transport: If you select this mode, it prioritizes public transport, listing all the available transit options. In some cities, Apple Maps also supports timing and much more.
- Ride: Using this icon, you can find the ride options. Using this icon, you can find the ride options.
- Cycling: It shows cycling directions.
- Starting Point: You can set the trip starting point using this location.
- Destination: You can set the destination using this option.
- Reorder Stops: If you have added any places in between, you can reorder them; you can simply drag their position.
- Voice Input: You can just add a stop using your voice note.
- Add Stop: You can add another stop.
Apple Maps Add Pin Screen
This screen appears when you are trying to pin a new place. You can tap on the add plus option under the places section.
- Confirm Pin: Once you select the location, you can tap on this to confirm and save the location.
- Voice Search: Search the place using the voice note.
- Pin Suggestion: Apple also offers some pin suggestions if you want to.
- Search: You can search for a place and pin it.
- Siri Suggestions: You can view the Siri suggestions based on your past location history and the places you frequently visit.
Apple Maps Navigation Screen
- Current Position: This icon shows your live location.
- Share ETA: It lets you share your estimated arrival time (ETA) with others.
- Trip Details: Shows the arrival time, travel time, distance, and more.
- Navigation Instruction: This icon shows how to take the next route action.
Apple Maps Route Steps Screen
This screen appears if you tap on the route, which displays all your routes.
- Collapse Directions: It hides the turn list.
- Proceed to Route: Guides you back to the route.
Apple Maps Route Options Screen
This screen appears if you swipe up when you are navigating; it reveals more details about your trip.
- Route Stops: Shows stops and arrival times that you have set; you can also add a new stop.
- Add Stop: You can add a new stop.
- Share ETA: Share your arrival time, the same option that appears by default; you can tap on it to select the contacts of friends you want to share the ETA with.
- Report an Incident: You can report a road incident if you see any while you are navigating.
- Voice Controls: You can control the directions and all with your voice, especially useful if you don’t want to see the map while driving and get hands-free voice directions; remember it is not an assistant, it is one-way.
- End Route: Stop the navigation and quit the current navigation.
- Trip Summary: The same quick info that shows the ETA, travel time, and distance even if you swipe up.
Apple Maps Profile Menu Screen
This is the profile screen that appears if you tap on the profile option.
- Profile: This is your Apple Maps profile; it is basically your Apple ID profile that also appears here, listing your name and email.
- Close: You can use these icons to close the profile menu.
- Places: You can view your saved places.

'She's our hero': dog honoured after protecting Nipigon, Ont., family from black bear last fall
Bear burst into home last September
A dog from Nipigon, Ont., is being recognized for her efforts to protect her family from a black bear last fall.
Chloe, a mixed-breed, medium-sized dog, has been inducted into the Purina Animal Hall of Fame, which recognizes pets "for their remarkable bravery and unwavering devotion in protecting their owners during life-threatening emergencies," a media release states.
"She's a rescue dog," said Colette Shwetz, who owns Chloe along with her husband, Joe. "We rescued her in May 2019. She was about six months old when she came to us."
"She doesn't like a lot of attention. She's just one of those old soul dogs," Colette Shwetz said, adding "she's just full of love."
That was certainly on full display the night of Sept. 16, 2025. Chloe was let out into the yard, and when she came back in, the bear followed.
"Here we are in my kitchen, the three of us, me, the dog and the bear," Colette Shwetz said.
Joe Shwetz was already asleep, but was woken up by Chloe's barking.
"I got up, run out, went into the kitchen," Joe Shwetz said. "Chloe had a hind leg, which was the bear, in her mouth, trying to pull it towards the door."
All three managed to get the bear out of the kitchen and into an adjoining hallway, and it then made its way into the basement.
Held off the bear until police arrived
Chloe "stood guard," Colette Shwetz said, barking and holding the bear off until the police arrived and dispatched it.
"We all ended up with a lot of staples and stitches and a lot of wound care," Colette Shwetz said. "Chloe, we almost lost her through the bite that she got, but she did really well. We got her through it."
And Chloe also got a steak dinner as a reward, Colette Shwetz said.
"She's our hero," she said. "I know that without her, I would not be here. That is a 100 per cent certainty."
In a media release, Purina said the hall of fame was established in 1968, and has so far recognized 198 animals — 170 dogs, 27 cats, and one horse — "for extraordinary acts of courage and devotion that have helped save lives across Canada."
Chloe isn't the only dog from northwestern Ontario in the hall of fame.
Murph, an Australian Blue Merle Sheepdog from Kenora, was inducted in 1984 after she alerted her owners to a fire in the apartment building they were living in.
Her owners then rushed to notify all the other residents, and all escaped the fire.

NATO’s Nightmare
The U.S. and Europe have no clear plan for a joint attack from Russia and China.
Western military planners do not seem eager to talk about their nightmare scenario, much less prepare for it. But they tend to agree on how it would begin: a coordinated, near-simultaneous attack on opposite sides of the planet, in which Russia targets a NATO member in Eastern Europe while China makes its move against Taiwan. The U.S. military would need to react on two fronts at once—three if it remains at war in the Middle East.
Until recently, this possibility sat at the more outlandish end of the threat spectrum, somewhere between a loose nuke and an alien invasion. Synchronized attacks would require a conspiracy too big for Beijing and Moscow to hide. Satellites would see their forces getting into position, giving the United States and its allies time to rally their defenses.
About a year ago, General Alexus Grynkewich, the top NATO commander in Europe, issued a rare public warning about the risk of a two-front war against Russia and China, and he called on European allies to help the U.S. prepare. But when I asked a range of military experts and strategists what the West would do in such a situation, the responses rang surprisingly hollow. Most of them expressed bewilderment and a bit of shame about how little has been done in recent years to study this risk in detail.
“Let’s just say this is the scenario we’re currently not ready for,” Florence Gaub, the director of the research division at the NATO Defense College, one of the alliance’s main academies for officers, in Rome, told me. NATO strategists remain “keenly aware” of this gap in their planning, Gaub, who specializes in the forecasting and analysis of future threats, said. But they have not taken steps to fill that gap.
Even as Russia and China have intensified their military cooperation, the West has held only a few low-profile exercises to analyze what would happen if the two launched a joint attack. Public discussion of this possibility has been remarkably muted among Western experts and military brass, who seem to lack the theoretical frameworks to process such a calamity and game out a response.
Mark Montgomery, a retired rear admiral of the U.S. Navy and a frequent participant in high-profile war games and strategic-planning exercises, told me that he and his colleagues last studied the idea of a two-front war against Russia and China roughly 15 years ago. “It didn’t go well,” he said.
Back then, the exercises showed that the U.S. did not have the weapons stockpiles or the industrial capacity to sustain a lengthy period of fighting on multiple fronts, and it could not rely on its allies to pick up the slack. Since then, Montgomery said, “Every one of those metrics has gone down. None of them has gotten better.” Under pressure from the Trump administration, U.S. allies have increased their defense spending. “But their forces have not yet shown improvement.”
The other sides have. Although Russia has been failing to achieve its objectives in the war in Ukraine, it has succeeded in shifting its enormous industrial base onto a war footing, and formerly civilian factories now aid in the production of missiles and tanks. The Russian experience in Ukraine has also made its forces adept at drone warfare. China, which produces most of the world’s drones, has not fought a war in decades and suffers from corruption in its upper ranks. But it has overtaken the U.S. in the number of warships and long-range missiles in its arsenal. Russia and China have also built stronger ties between their militaries under what their leaders describe as a “no-limits” partnership.
From their vantage point, the window of opportunity to strike the West might never have looked more tantalizing. The U.S. remains bogged down in Iran, having pulled a lot of its ships and aircraft out of Asia and Europe to backfill its forces in the Middle East. An estimated two-thirds of the American arsenal of advanced air-defense missiles has been depleted since February, and Donald Trump’s persistent insults and threats against NATO have turned the rift between the U.S. and its allies into a yawning chasm.
For most of his tenure as Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin has aspired to dismantle NATO, and its current moment of weakness offers him a rare chance to achieve that goal. He has already started testing its defenses. NATO members in Eastern Europe, such as Romania, Poland, and the Baltic states, have seen repeated violations of their air space by Russian drones, missiles, and fighter jets. Earlier this month, German authorities found a suspected Russian drone loaded with explosives at an airport in Leipzig, apparently preparing to blow up a Ukrainian cargo plane over NATO territory.
The most recent U.S.-intelligence assessments have reportedly concluded that Russia could try to test NATO’s resolve in the next few years, using a cyberattack or a small-scale incursion against a member of the alliance. Such a gambit would be more likely to succeed in weakening NATO if Russia timed it to coincide with a Chinese attack on Taiwan, Admiral Rob Bauer, a former chair of the alliance’s Military Committee, told me. As of last January, when he retired from NATO leadership, Bauer was not aware of any concerted effort inside the alliance to prepare a strategy for this “worst-case scenario,” as he called it. “What are we going to do? Who’s getting which troops?” Bauer asked. “I think it would be wise to think that through.”
Many military threats have seemed far-fetched until they happened. Before the Nazi invasion of the Soviet Union, in 1941, Joseph Stalin received repeated warnings from his own generals and spies. But he refused to believe them until the bombing started, hindering the ability of his forces to prepare. The U.S. likewise failed to prepare for the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor. In the lead-up to the First World War, Europe split into two rival alliances, and no one predicted the scale of the destruction that their conflict would unleash.
“The indications were clear that they would clash, and we just weren’t ready for it,” David Santoro, the president and CEO of the Pacific Forum, a research institute in Hawaii that focuses on Indo-Pacific security issues, told me. In 2023, Santoro and his team organized a round of theoretical war games, known as tabletop exercises, in which two American allies called for help at the same time: Taiwan came under attack from China while North Korea seized its chance to invade South Korea. “We were struggling to keep up and divide labor,” Santoro recalled. “And we weren’t even talking about Europe. I can only imagine what would happen if you threw Russia in there.”
A great variety of tabletop exercises happen all the time. Most involve two teams of military experts sitting around a conference table and responding to one another’s moves, like a multiplayer chess game. The organizers try to keep the rules simple and clearly defined. Such tight parameters do not reflect the chaos of warfare, but they prevent the games from getting too hectic when players from different fields of research talk past one another. This bias toward orderly games helps explain why so little research has been done on what experts call “multi-crisis environments.” Almost by definition, such scenarios would quickly get confusing.
“It’s complicated, to be sure, but I don’t think it is too complicated to study,” Eric Heginbotham, an authority on war-gaming at MIT’s Security Studies Program, told me. “I just don’t believe that anyone has done it.” He cautioned that some secretive department within the Pentagon or elsewhere may have quietly analyzed this grim contingency and drawn up response plans.
The general topic of a two-front war now gets discussed among military experts “more than it used to be,” he said. The Center for Strategic and International Studies, a think tank in Washington, D.C., published a lengthy report in June on the best ways for the U.S. to “counter an axis led by China and Russia.” But Heginbotham, who has worked closely with CSIS, said that none of the most prominent research institutes in the U.S. and Europe has organized war games on the subject. “You’d need two relatively big and elaborate games running simultaneously, with some sort of command authority setting priorities in the middle,” he said in an email. “Sounds very interesting.”
In the public statements of senior NATO leaders, the risk of a multifront war has come up over the past year or so, though not very often. In December, a few months after Grynkewich issued his warning to U.S. allies, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte mentioned the threat at the end of an interview that he gave to a German newspaper. “China is looking at Taiwan,” Rutte said. “And I am convinced that if China takes military action there, it will pressure its junior partner, Russia, under Putin’s leadership, to keep us busy here in Europe.”
One of the most detailed analyses of this possibility, at least in the public domain, comes from an obscure research institute in Prague called the European Values Center for Security Policy. Its 35-year-old director, Jakub Janda, told me that he began studying the idea of a “dual-theater” war in Europe and Asia after the institute opened an outpost in Taipei, in January 2022. At the time, the risk of a coordinated attack from Russia and China seemed remote or, as Janda put it, “not a major consideration.”
That began to change the following month, when Russian tanks rolled into Ukraine. Putin had visited Beijing less than three weeks before he ordered the invasion. He has since made at least four more visits to China, and another one is planned for November. Throughout this period, China has become the main supplier of technology to the Russian weapons industry while propping up the Russian economy through the purchase of oil and gas. Although they have no mutual-defense pact, Russia and China hold regular military drills to help keep their forces in sync.
The first war game to simulate a joint attack from both of them took place at Janda’s institute in the spring of 2024. Finding experts with enough background knowledge to participate proved difficult for him. Most research institutions and think tanks have separate teams that specialize in their own regions, he said. “They work in their silos, with different expertise.”
Over time, the participants grasped the way that wars in Asia and Europe could overlap and reinforce one another. The institute has already held roughly 20 rounds of war games on this topic, gathering experts in a variety of countries, including Japan and South Korea. The results have been particularly alarming, Janda said, for the Europeans. In almost every two-front scenario that he has studied, the U.S. prioritizes the Chinese threat and transfers military resources from Europe to Asia, leaving its NATO allies to defend themselves against Russia.
In one hypothetical case, China begins the war slowly by banning the export of raw materials to Europe’s defense sector. It maintains the embargo for five months, long enough for European factories to run out of supplies and stop producing weapons. Then Russia, with full access to Chinese resources, invades a NATO ally in Eastern Europe.
All of the scenarios in Janda’s series laid bare the need for Western unity. In the event of a Chinese attack on Taiwan, for example, the U.S. might demand that Europe impose severe sanctions on China’s economy, effectively cutting off trade. “But European governments don’t want to do that,” Janda said, describing how that premise played out among the experts. “The problem with European capitals is that Taiwan is far away. They want to focus on the threat from Russia, and that’s what scares me.”
If Russia and China act in unison while the U.S. bickers with its allies, the chances of a Western victory in a two-front war begin to look bleak. The side that comes out on top, in other words, tends to be the one that moves with common purpose and remains united over time.

Why positive cocaine test could mean end of Kyrgios' career
- Published
Nick Kyrgios once said there was "zero chance" he would be playing tennis into his 30s.
But it was at the age of 31, while attempting another comeback from serious knee and wrist injuries, that he tested positive for a metabolite of cocaine at June's Mallorca Open.
In a post on social media, Kyrgios said it was a "huge mistake" for which he takes full responsibility.
But he added that recent injuries - he has only played eight tournaments and won two matches since the start of 2023 - have taken a huge toll on him.
"Coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined," he added.
Kyrgios will not be able to play until his case is resolved because of a mandatory provisional suspension.
But although he faces a potential ban of up to four years, his suspension would be limited to a maximum of three months if he can prove the drug was taken out of competition.
The Australian has achieved more than most on the sporting stage. As a 19-year-old in 2014 he stunned then world number one Rafael Nadal on his Centre Court debut, and finished runner-up at Wimbledon eight years later.
At his best, Kyrgios is a flamboyant and athletic shot-maker with flair, touch and an explosive game.
But he can also be destructive and verbally abusive, and has regularly struggled to sustain the levels of professionalism and abstinence needed for a prolonged stay at the very top.
In 2015, Kyrgios was given a suspended 28-day ban for making lewd remarks about Stan Wawrinka's girlfriend during a match in Montreal.
A year later, he was banned for eight weeks for his behaviour - including a "lack of best effort" - at the Shanghai Masters. This was reduced to three weeks after he agreed to consult a sports psychologist.
2019 was the nadir. Kyrgios was defaulted from a match at the Italian Open for hurling a chair on to the court, and was later fined $113,000 for verbally abusing umpire Fergus Murphy in Cincinnati.
The ATP later issued a suspended 16-week ban for a "pattern of behaviour related to his verbal abuse of officials and/or spectators" over the previous 12 months.
Kyrgios described 2019 as the "lowest point of my career" when interviewed for Netflix's Break Point documentary series.
"I was drinking, abusing drugs. I lost my relationship with my family, pushed all my close friends away," he said.
"Being bullied at a young age for being short and fat and brown scarred me for sure."
Kyrgios said he wore a compression sleeve to cover up self-harming scars on his arm and spent time in a psychiatric hospital in London to try and "figure out my problems".
He separately spoke about being forced out of a pub in Wimbledon Village by his agent in the early hours of a match day, and told Louis Theroux in 2024 that he would sometimes have "20 to 30 drinks" before playing the next day.
He has confessed to playing too much basketball - including for an hour before he beat David Ferrer in the 2017 Cincinnati Masters semi-finals - and has often said he has been unable to "dedicate" his life to tennis.
"I just enjoy doing whatever I'm doing," he said.
"I don't eat well. I don't train just for tennis, I train just for a general happy living - I know it sounds ridiculous, but I play a bit of tennis on the side."
In 2023, Kyrgios admitted assaulting ex-girlfriend Chiara Passari by pushing her on the pavement during a row in Canberra. The magistrate called the incident "a single act of stupidity or frustration" when sparing him a criminal record.
Then two years ago he publicly distanced himself from controversial influencer Andrew Tate, who is currently fighting extradition to the UK on charges including rape and offences related to sex trafficking.
Kyrgios told the BBC he had "deleted posts, unfollowed him and gone to all lengths to distance" himself from Tate.
The current world number 919 will now step away from public life for the next 28 days to "do the work and come back better".
The legal process could take many months - and Kyrgios is no fan of tennis' anti-doping system.
Describing the system as "awful," he made clear repeatedly his opinion that both Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek received overly lenient bans after their recent high-profile doping cases.
"Sad day for tennis. Fairness in tennis does not exist," Kyrgios wrote after Sinner accepted a three-month ban for testing positive for clostebol.
But if he does decide he wants to continue his career into his 30s, much will rest on the process of which Kyrgios has been so critical.

The story so far: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has now become the deadliest in the country’s history as deaths cross 2,300 mark as of August 18, 2026.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the outbreak is on track to surpass the 2014-16 outbreak in West Africa, the deadliest on record with over 28,616 cases and 11,325 deaths. As cases and deaths mount, the strife-torn DRC is struggling to contain the spread of the deadly disease.
What is the latest situation?
The country has reported over 2,325 deaths, exceeding the toll of 2,299 reported in the previous outbreak, according to the WHO. The fatality rate has increased to nearly 47%. The number of confirmed cases stood at 4,945, including the 101 new cases detected in the previous 24 hours. Around 1,040 people have recovered and while 730 are still hospitalised or in isolation.
This ebola outbreak — the 17th in the country — spread to a sixth province with a death reported in Bas-uele. While Ituri still shoulders a heavy burden with a maximum number of cases, the disease has also affected people in North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo provinces.
It was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern by the WHO three months ago.
Why is the outbreak causing concern?
The current outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus which does not have any approved vaccines or treatments.
Authorities then have to rely on identifying cases to check transmission. The ongoing rebel conflict, inadequate health surveillance and other facilities, deep distrust in authorities, burial practices which involve touching of the body (Ebloa spreads through contact with blood or bodily fluids of a person infected with or has died of disease), misinformation regarding ebola has severely impeded containment efforts.
A recent strike by health care workers at the epicentre of the outbreak over payment dues also added to the woes. Working in the front-lines, these workers have also been attacked by rebels and crowds which is a big cause of concern amid a deadly outbreak.
The WHO has warned that the outbreak is “outpacing the response”. “We are chasing the virus, the virus is ahead of us,” WHO Africa director Dr Mohamed Janabi said while the United Nations warned that the epidemic was now killing one person every 30 minutes.
Why does detection matter in this outbreak?
Amid UN’s warning that the Bundibugyo outbreak is taking lives at a much faster rate, experts stress the need for quick detection and rapid contact tracing.
“..we’re still seeing many cases detected very late, when treatment is less likely to succeed, with many identified only after they die in the community,” said Thomas Parisch, a public health specialist recently deployed to DRC with Medecins Sans Frontieres
Though the outbreak was formally declared on May 15, WHO says genetic sequencing showed that the virus had actually begun circulating in February. The country’s Health Minister had earlier cited the case of first-reported death and the subsequent delays as a cause for escalation of the spread of the disease.
Sounding concern, WHO Director-General said on August 17, 2026, “What worries me most is where people are dying – at home, in their communities, outside treatment centres, and outside known contact lists. Every death like that signals a chain of transmission we have not yet found.”
“Until each chain is broken, the outbreak continues – and the risk does not stop at the DRC’s borders,” he added.
What is being done to contain the outbreak?
The WHO has been working alongside local authorities to step up surveillance and containment efforts. It has also been working to expand the number of treatment centers and training workers to staff these centers.
Clinical trials for two possible treatments began earlier in DRC while various firms are also evaluating and developing vaccines for the strain.
UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher recently announced the allocation of an additional $30.5 million and the deployment of 20 more staff to aid the response on the frontlines.
“We need speed, scale and solidarity before this virus gets even further ahead of us,” he said
Experts have cited the need to close diagnostic gaps and the need for sustained regional diagnostic and genomic surveillance to identify outbreaks.

The USS Abraham Lincoln is an aircraft carrier for the United States Navy with a long, storied history. The vessel first launched in the late 1980s, and it soon became a crucial asset in operations such as Desert Storm, Enduring Freedom, Iraqi Freedom and more, including the recent conflict with Iran dubbed Operation Epic Fury.
While the ship's legendary status was touted on official channels, reports circulated about grim conditions aboard the ship during its latest deployment, which began in November 2025 and was originally supposed to conclude in May 2026, according to the Navy Times. In July, the USS Abraham Lincoln set a new record for consecutive days at sea.
However, in August, the BBC reported "food shortages, broken plumbing and exhaustion" and attempts by crew members to jump overboard. Concern was so great that Navy officials even met with the families of the deployed service members in a meeting rife with concerns for "the sailors' mental health, safety on deck, a lack of supplies, food shortages, water contamination and disruptions in the mail system," according to MS NOW.
With the storied aircraft carrier front and center in headlines, we put together this collection of investigations regarding some of these recent claims — as well as a few far-older claims from the Snopes archives that involved some of the vessel's previous deployments.

Malda Medical College security manager arrested on guard's repeated rape charge
A security guard at Malda Medical College and Hospital has accused a security agency manager of repeated rape and threats. The case has raised fresh concerns over workplace safety for women at public institutions.
A security guard deployed at Malda Medical College and Hospital has accused a security agency manager of repeatedly raping her and threatening her with serious consequences if she disclosed the alleged abuse.
The accused, identified as Shubhankar Laskar, is the facility manager of the private agency responsible for providing security services at the hospital. Following a complaint filed by the woman, police arrested Laskar and launched an investigation into the allegations.
According to the complaint, the woman alleged that she was sexually assaulted multiple times at the security agency’s office located near the hospital’s diarrhoea ward. She also claimed that the accused threatened her to prevent her from reporting the incidents to anyone.
The victim lodged a complaint at the English Bazar Police Station in Malda on August 16. Acting on the complaint, police initiated an inquiry and subsequently arrested the accused.
Laskar was produced before a court on Wednesday, police said. Investigators are now examining the allegations and gathering evidence as part of the ongoing probe.
The incident has triggered concerns over the safety and security of personnel working within the premises of the state-run medical institution.
Responding to the development, Malda Medical College and Hospital's Medical Superintendent-cum-Vice Principal (MSVP), Prosenjit Bor, said the arrest was made based on a rape complaint filed with the police.
“The police have arrested the accused on the basis of a rape complaint. I do not know the details of what exactly happened. The matter is under police investigation,” Bor said.
Police officials have not yet disclosed further details about the case but confirmed that the investigation is underway.
The case comes amid renewed scrutiny of workplace safety and protection mechanisms for women employed in hospitals and other public institutions. Authorities are expected to record statements from relevant witnesses and review evidence as part of the investigation.

“Please don’t let this be the final whistle for Jamshedpur FC,” the defender Pratik Chaudhari said, looking into the camera as teammates looked on disconsolately. “We would like to say on behalf of all the players, please do rethink about this. Because if this happens, this is not just a loss for Indian football … this is a big loss for all of India.”
In addition, fans of the Indian Super League club marched in protest, petitions were launched, and the Indian football legend Sunil Chhetri said it was a “punch to the gut” and joined others in begging for a rethink.
The target of all these pleas was the Jamshedpur owner Tata Steel, which surprisingly pulled the plug on the club on 31 July. After the problems of the 2025-26 campaign, which started five months late and lasted just 13 games, the new season’s big kick-off on 4 September was to be a new start. The positivity and optimism before the new season, fragile though it was, disappeared along with JFC.
And understandably so as it is a huge blow, for players, staff and fans but also for the league. Jamshedpur had solid support and won the ISL shield in 2022, five years after the club was formed. Steve Coppell was the first head coach with Scott Cooper, Aidy Boothroyd and Owen Coyle all following in his footsteps.
Baljit Rihal of Inventive Sports was the agent who took Coppell to the city in the eastern state of Jharkhand. “To be quite frank, after all the uncertainty Indian football has faced over the last couple of seasons, Jamshedpur FC would have been one of the last clubs I expected to pull out,” he told the Guardian.
The club was founded by the Tata Group, which has been involved with Indian football at various levels for decades. “When an institution with that history decides it can no longer continue at the highest level, it says something very serious about the current state of the game,” Rihal said.
The league is also losing a major corporate backer, one which insists, however, that the decision is not about money. “At Tata Steel, sports have never been evaluated through a profit-and-loss lens,” the company’s vice-president and the club’s chairman, Sundara Ramam, told the Guardian.
“Our decision to exit professional club football has nothing to do with Tata Steel’s financial position. In fact, the resources that would have been spent on the club will continue to be invested in grassroots sports development. Our sports budget is not decreasing. It will continue to grow. As chairman of Jamshedpur FC, I can say clearly that this decision was driven by our desire to focus more intensely on grassroots development and not by financial considerations.”
Yet if others follow suit then there may not be much of a professional pathway for young talent. This latest episode shines a light on the league once more. In the club’s original letter sent to the All India Football Federation, concerns were expressed about the financial model of the ISL, which recently changed. Reliance Industries was the federation’s commercial partner from 2010 but, when that agreement expired in 2025, a new deal was not made and a new partner not found, hence the shortened season.
This time, the AIFF looks after governance and administration with the clubs taking on the commercial and marketing side. “The old model meant clubs had very little say in how the league was packaged and sold,” Ravi Puskur, the chief executive of Goa FC, said last month.
“Now the clubs hold the broadcast and sponsorship rights directly. It puts the incentive to grow the league’s commercial value in the hands of the people who are most invested in it growing.”
A member of Jamshedpur’s staff told the Guardian that the decision was because of concerns over the new arrangements. “I believe Tata are not interested in the club-led model,” he says. “There had to be a commitment of four years and the AIFF was asking for an initial payment of around £43,000 from all 14 clubs to be made by 31 July. Tata might have thought it’s better to stop rather than get dragged into unknown waters.”
It is a worrying exit as this is not the only corporate departure from Indian football of late. “Reliance stepping away from its central role was significant,” Rihal says. “City Football Group leaving Mumbai City was another warning.” That happened in December, in the middle of the problems last season. “Tata now withdrawing from Jamshedpur FC feels different again because of the group’s deep-rooted history in Indian football. These departures have happened for different reasons, but collectively they represent a major loss of confidence in the professional game.”
Now there is fear that others may follow and there will be some relief if all 13 remaining clubs kick off the season. “Indian football can recover, but we should not underestimate the scale of the challenge,” Rihal says.
“The priority now must be the people affected, followed by urgent clarity over the league’s structure and future. Players, staff and supporters cannot continue living from one period of uncertainty to the next. They deserve much better.”
There is still hope that Tata could have a rethink. “I understand that some tough decisions in sport are down to what makes sense in the boardroom,” Chhetri said. “But I can only request and hope that the thinktank at Tata picks their heart over head and reconsiders this call. It might be a poor business decision, but it will be the one Indian football needs the most at this hour.”

You can customize websites without coding by using AI to create Tampermonkey user scripts or custom browser extensions. These tools can change fonts, remove clutter, tweak layouts, add features, and apply your changes automatically whenever you visit a site.
We are in the era of personal software. Thanks to AI, anyone can now build fully functional tools as good as existing high-end software for their workflows.

Website owners should spend extra time tweaking to meet user needs.
Many websites that I personally follow and read have used AI to revamp their existing user interface, resulting in the same issues.
Fortunately, I found a way to easily customize website designs once the webpage is rendered. All changes I made to any website are temporary and can be easily reverted.
There are plenty of ways you can tweak website design; however, using extensions and user scripts are two best reliable ways. Those changes will auto-apply every time you visit the webpage.
In this guide, I am going to show you both methods, with step-by-step guides on how to tweak the design of any website.
How to Redesign and Personalize Any Website Without Coding
Just a heads-up: this might not work for every website. Some websites use hard-coded elements that are impossible to tweak, while others use completely different structures where you will need to try various approaches to get what you want without breaking anything.
Method 1: Customize Websites Using Tampermonkey User Scripts
The first method is using user scripts. You can run simple code snippets on your browser console once the web page is rendered. Since these user scripts only work once the website is fully rendered and stored locally on your device, once you refresh the page, everything goes back to normal. But to keep the changes permanently, you can use the Tampermonkey extension, which allows you to run multiple user scripts on any web page and every time you visit the site.
Tampermonkey is free to use. And since all the changes apply locally, you don’t need to worry about breaking everything. Even if it breaks, you can simply disable the added code.
You need to create a script that works for the specific site with all possible changes you want. I recommend using AI tools.
The best approach is to use an IDE where these AI models can directly inspect the website and analyze all the code. Alternatively, you can copy-paste the entire website HTML or the rendered code into any AI chat tool, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude, and ask it to generate a user script.

I have already covered the best user scripts that you can run on a browser, but since you are using AI, the possibilities are endless. You can change the font size, remove ads or images if the site loads slowly, change the action of specific elements (such as auto-loading pagination), and much more
Remember that you can also ask ChatGPT or other AI tools to specifically build a script for a specific website, especially if you only want to make changes related to that specific site and don’t want to apply those changes to every website. Once the code is generated, follow the steps to add it to Tampermonkey.

Step 1: First, go to the Google Chrome Web Store, search for the Tampermonkey extension, and tap on Add to Chrome.
Step 2: Now, pin the Tampermonkey extension.
Step 3: Next, you can tap on the extensions icon in the top toolbar and tap on the pin icon next to the Tampermonkey extension.
Step 4: Now tap on Tampermonkey and tap on the plus icon.
Step 5: From here, you can paste the user script that you have generated,
Step 6: Tap on the file option and tap on save.
Step 7: Now, the changes should be automatically applied to your browser. If not, you can tap on Tampermonkey again and click “Run Script” if it is not working by default.
You can also use Tampermonkey on your mobile browser; you can use a browser with extension support. Our favorite is the Quetta browser. You can see the detailed guide below on how to install third-party extensions on the Quetta browser.

Step 4: Now, from the options, tap on Create a new script and paste the script you created here. From here, tap on the file option and click on Save, and that’s it.
Step 5: Now, visit the website; the changes should be applied automatically.
Method 2: Customize Websites Using Browser Extensions
If you don’t want to use Tampermonkey, you can also create your own extension to make changes to any website. This is a recommended method for beginners.
Unlike Tampermonkey, which depends on user scripts, an extension is easier to access and manage. Moreover, you can also easily disable and enable extensions when you want. Plus, if you are an expert, you can also add additional features to the extensions, which is sometimes not possible with user scripts.
One catch here is that you need to build the extensions. You don’t need a programmer to do that. You need to pay for one of the tools, such as OpenAI Codex, Google Gemini, or Claude. If you are a programmer, you can build it yourself, but I wouldn’t recommend it, as using those AI tools makes it easier and faster to create any extensions.
For this guide, I am using Claude Code to create an extension. You can use any other AI model to do the same.
How to Add Your Custom Extension to Chrome
Step 1: First, open the Claude app on your Mac and switch to the Code tab.
Step 2: Under the Projects folder, create a new project folder named Extensions. Once created, simply enter the prompt for the extension you want to create.
Step 3: Here, I am creating a simple extension that allows me to increase or decrease the font sizes on any web page.
Step 4: The extension will be created in the same folder. But remember that there is a high chance that it does not work on the first attempt. You need to iterate and fix the issues that come up to get the desired output you want.
Step 5: Now, open the folder and find the extension folder.
Step 6: Now, to add the extension to your browser (let’s say for Google Chrome): Open settings, go to manage extension settings, and from here, enable developer options. Once enabled, tap on Load unpacked and select the extension folder. That’s it; the extension will be added to your extensions.
Remember, you can follow the same process on mobile too, using Quetta Browser (which you can watch in the detailed step-by-step video below).
To pin it, tap on the extensions icon at the top, select your extension, and tap on the pin option. If it doesn’t work, go back to Claude and review the extension instructions.
Describe the issues you are having with the extensions. You can also go to the browser console, copy everything in there, and paste it into Claude.
This will give you a better reference to find the exact issues the extension is having. Now, Claude will generate a new version of the extension. Follow the same process and load the same extension, and it will be replaced with the new extension version.
That’s it. Using Quetta browser, you can follow similar steps and use the extension on both the mobile and desktop versions. Since I have built the ability to resize the font, I can tap on the extension and adjust the font size on the web page.
Customize Websites Your Way
If you are fed up with your favorite website designs, this is how you can tweak and redesign websites from the user. The tweaks using user scripts and extensions may not work for every website.
